text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Questions surround Pol Pot case: Charter, immigration rights may not allow Canada to hold Khmer Rouge leader for prosecution.
- Russia moves to curb religions: Rights restricted for Protestant sects.
- Ontario suspends privatizing efforts: Union pact being broken, rulings say.
- Handover anxiety sparks Hong Kong shopping spree: Retailers peddle Chinese chic to a people with identity crisis.
- Private care no cure, British say: A London hospital offers queue-jumping to the affluent, but its chief executive doesn't recommend the plan to Canada.
- Royal eyes takeover of insurer: Canada's biggest bank said close to buying biggest insurance firm - Edper's London Life.
- Black fails in quest to take Southam private: Hollinger retains control but won't have free access to cash.
- Rate fears send Dow plunging: Japan PM talks of selling U.S. bonds.
- Husky, Alberta Energy plan C$400-million heavy oil line: 552 kilometres of pipe to carry output from a dozen firms.
- Hashimoto's words stampede jittery Wall Street.
- Hollinger loses bid for rest of Southam: But Conrad Black's poker game with holdout shareholders isn't over.
